correctness.rationale: For even n,k, exterior incidence operators give A^2=0 and rank(A)=binomial(n-2,k-1). The two endpoint basis vectors and their A-images form a provably independent four-space U; B maps this space explicitly as (b+c,a+d,a,b), with B^3 swapping each paired coordinate, hence cycles of lengths 1,3,6 in exact counts 1,1,2. B^2=AE+EA+E^2 maps the entire space onto U, proving global transient at most two. The symmetric-rank/direct-sum argument shows rank B=r+2; kernel-preimage dimensions yield exact C0,C1,C2. Full enumeration of 65,600 configurations for (4,2),(6,2),(6,4), and exact rank checks at nine graph sizes, agreed with the proof. Experiments alone are not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The p=2 rank and square-zero behaviour of the unmodified Johnson adjacency graph are explicitly known from Peeters (2002) and are attributed. Novelty assessed only for the precisely proved one-edge-deletion instability: 16 periodic states, primitive 3/6 cycle census, exact two-step transient depths. Relevant primary full text, semantically retrieved nearby published mathematics and accessible historical findings were compared by logical implication, not by title. No identified stronger coverage; unindexed equivalent work and one inaccessible code-paper full text remain risks. This is bounded rather than certified novelty.
residual_risks: An unindexed or inaccessible study of binary orbit dynamics on Johnson graphs after deleting one edge could already imply the exact three- and six-cycle census.
The 2015 Fish Johnson-graph code paper was not examined in full and is not treated as evidence of noncoverage.
The older 1994 Peeters memorandum was available by abstract and institutional bibliographic description; the later 2002 full article was inspected for the specific Johnson rank formulas.

value.rationale: A single missing link changes the original nilpotent all-to-zero map into a system with guaranteed 3- and 6-cycles, a qualitative dynamical robustness failure for all even-even Johnson graphs. The theorem gives the entire recurrent census and exact finite-volume transient populations rather than a numerical example or a routine restatement of an existing binary-rank table. The defect-induced four-dimensional invariant subspace offers a structural explanation and makes the result reusable for comparison with other local perturbations.
